title: reading-notes-llm-inference-lucas-hernandez
body:
Quick reading notes / scratchpad - focus on practical takeaways for Redwood runtime and experiments to run.

Context
- Goal: reduce p99 latency and per-token cost for multi-tenant hosted API while keeping quality (no hallucinations).
- Workload: mix of short chat turns (avg 120 tokens) and long context docs (2k-8k). Need good KV cache behavior + graceful fallback.

Papers / links skimmed
- FlashAttention (arXiv 2023): key implementation ideas: tiling attention compute to reduce memory, re-ordering ops to stream GPU memory. Good for long contexts; large speedups on fp16 and bf16.
- Key-Value cache eviction strategies blog post (internal link CONFLUENCE-1234): suggests LRU-ish per-shard eviction + pinning for hot prefixes.
- Quantization notes (8-bit papers): mixed results for causal LM; per-channel quantization + outlier handling seems necessary.

Main takeaways for runtime
- Kernel selection: switch to FlashAttention-like kernels for >4k seq length; fallback to standard for short sequences to avoid overhead. Implement a cheap heuristic: if seq_len * batch_size > threshold then route to tiled kernel.
- KV cache eviction: per-client TTL + MRU pinning for conversational prefixes. When mem pressure, evict least recently used across low-traffic tenants first (maintain tenant-weighted priority).
- Batching: continuous batching with max-wait=8ms gave best tail for interactive tests. For throughput workloads, allow batch accumulation up to 64 tokens or 4 requests. Need per-customer override via policy.
- Quantization: try GPTQ-style post-training quantization on small model variants; avoid aggressive 4-bit for high-precision tasks (code, math). Keep model variants exposed as "fast" vs "accurate" with routing policy.

Experiments to run (priority order)
1) Microbench: FlashAttention vs baseline on A100 for seq_len=4096, batch sizes [1,4,8,16]. Measure latency, memory, and p99.
2) KV cache: simulate mixed workload with 1k tenants, spike traffic for 10% of tenants; evaluate eviction policies (LRU, FIFO, tenant-weighted) and impact on latency for pinned prefixes.
3) Batching params: run latency SLO tests with different max-wait (2ms, 8ms, 20ms) and max-batch-size; record cost-per-token and p99.
4) Quantization: produce 8-bit checkpoints for small model (7B) and run evals on code/math benchmark; compare regression vs baseline 16-bit.

Open questions / risks
- FlashAttention integration complexity with our kernel/graph compiler and multi-GPU KV cache sharding (need to ensure kernel streams align with sharded kv layout).
- Eviction fairness: tenant-weighted eviction could starve small tenants if implemented badly. Need simulation and maybe credit system.
- Model quality: quantization can shift logits subtly and break safety classifiers - need evals tied to alerts in Redwood Optimize.

Notes to self / action items
- Reach out to Maya for existing FlashAttention PoC (she mentioned a draft PR).
- File microbench harness under serving-runtime/perf/microbench and link PR in ticket JIRA-9812.
- Draft short doc for infra team: kv-cache eviction design + metrics to expose (cache hit rate, eviction rate, tenant impact).

References / misc
- Consider ICLR 2025 talks on long-context models (bookmark for follow-up).
- Add a short section to Redwood Optimize eval harness to detect quantization regressions automatically.

Unresolved
- Need to decide threshold heuristic for kernel switch (empirically driven).
- How to persist eviction policy state across restarts? Look into lightweight on-disk metadata or central config service.

End of notes.
